page.text:
In mathematical practice, sets are rarely specified by exhaustive
enumeration. Instead, they are defined through *comprehension* (or
set-builder) notation, which specifies a predicate characterizing
membership: $$\{x \in A : \varphi(x)\}$$ Here $\varphi$ is a predicate on
sets, and the Axiom Schema of Separation guarantees that the collection
of all elements in the preexisting set $A$ satisfying $\varphi$ forms a
legitimate set. For finite sets, we retain the familiar roster notation
$\{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n\}$.
